'''Ana Maria Cuervo''' (born 14 July 1966) is a Spanish-American physician, researcher, and cell biologist. She is a distinguished professor in developmental and [[molecular biology]] and [[medicine]] and co-director of the Institute for Geroscience at the [[Albert Einstein College of Medicine]]. She is best known for her research work on [[autophagy]], the process by which cells recycle waste products, and its changes in aging and age-related diseases.

==Biography==
Cuervo was born in Barcelona, Spain, on 14 July 1966. She studied medicine at the [[University of Valencia]] in 1986 and further pursued a PhD in [[biochemistry]] and [[molecular biology]] under the mentorship of Erwin Knecht, a biochemist studying [[lysosome]]s and [[proteosome]] at the time.<ref name="Scientist">{{cite news |last1=SCUDELLARI |first1=MEGAN |title=Waste-Management Consultant |url=https://www.the-scientist.com/profile/waste-management-consultant-38483 |accessdate=27 July 2018 |work=The Scientist Magazine® |date=1 November 2013 |language=en}}</ref> In 1993, she published her first academic paper as a co-author on lysosomal degradation which challenged the assumption that it was non-specific.<ref>{{cite journal |last1=Aniento |first1=F |last2=Roche |first2=E |last3=Cuervo |first3=AM |last4=Knecht |first4=E |title=Uptake and degradation of glyceraldehyde-3-phosphate dehydrogenase by rat liver lysosomes. |journal=The Journal of Biological Chemistry |date=15 May 1993 |volume=268 |issue=14 |pages=10463–70 |doi=10.1016/S0021-9258(18)82222-0 |pmid=8486700 |doi-access=free }}</ref> Cuervo also worked with Fred “Paulo” Dice of [[Tufts University]] on lysosomes during the summer months as Spanish labs were closed during this time of year. Cuervo later accepted a full-time post-doctorate position at Dice's laboratory and focused on understanding this selective lysosomal degradation pathway. From 1994 to 2000, Cuervo and Dice published their findings on this pathway, identified the lysosomal membrane protein LAMP2A as the receptor for this form of autophagy and termed it [[chaperone-mediated autophagy|chaperone-mediated autophagy (CMA)]].<ref>{{Cite journal|last1=Cuervo|first1=A. M.|last2=Dice|first2=J. F.|date=1996-07-26|title=A receptor for the selective uptake and degradation of proteins by lysosomes|journal=Science|volume=273|issue=5274|pages=501–503|issn=0036-8075|pmid=8662539|doi=10.1126/science.273.5274.501|bibcode=1996Sci...273..501C |s2cid=42850597 }}</ref><ref>{{cite journal |last1=Cuervo |first1=Ana Maria |last2=Dice |first2=J. Fred |title=Age-related Decline in Chaperone-mediated Autophagy |journal=Journal of Biological Chemistry |date=6 October 2000 |volume=275 |issue=40 |pages=31505–31513 |doi=10.1074/jbc.M002102200 |pmid=10806201 |language=en |issn=0021-9258|doi-access=free }}</ref>

In October 2001, Cuervo accepted a faculty position at the [[Albert Einstein College of Medicine]] in [[The Bronx]], [[New York (state)|New York]]<nowiki/>where she continues primarily focused on chaperone-mediated autophagy and its role in aging and human disease.

== Academic and scientific activities ==
Cuervo is the co-director of the [https://einsteinmed.edu/centers/geroscience/research Einstein Institute for Aging Research] and a member of the Einstein Liver Research Center and Cancer Center. She is also the [[Robert A. Belfer|Robert]] and Renée Belfer Chair for the Study of [[Neurodegenerative Diseases]] at Albert Einstein College of Medicine. In 2015 she was elected International Academic of the Royal Academy of Medicine of the Valencia Community,  in 2017 member of the [[Real Academia de Ciencias Exactas, Físicas y Naturales|Real Academia de Ciencias Exactas, Fisicas y Naturales]] and in 2021 member of the [[Royal National Academy of Pharmacy (Spain)|Royal Academy of Farmacy]] in Spain. Dr. Cuervo is also one of the funding members of the [https://academyofgeroscience.org/ Academy of Geroscience]. In 2018, Cuervo was elected a member of the [[American Academy of Arts and Sciences]]<ref>{{cite web |title=Ana Maria Cuervo, M.D., Ph.D., is Elected to the American Academy of Arts and Sciences |url=http://www.einstein.yu.edu/news/releases/1294/ana-maria-cuervo-m-d--ph-d--is-elected-to-the-american-academy-of-arts-and-sciences/ |website=Albert Einstein College of Medicine |accessdate=28 July 2018 |archive-date=28 July 2018 |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20180728131443/http://www.einstein.yu.edu/news/releases/1294/ana-maria-cuervo-m-d--ph-d--is-elected-to-the-american-academy-of-arts-and-sciences/ |url-status=dead }}</ref> and in 2019 to the [[National Academy of Sciences]]. 

She has also served as a member of the  National Institute on Aging (NIA) Scientific Council, [[National Institute of Health|NIH]] Scientific Council of Councils, NIA Board of Scientific Counselors and in the Advisory Committee to the NIH Deputy Director.<ref>{{cite web |title=Ana Maria Cuervo MD, PhD |url=https://www.michaeljfox.org/foundation/researchers.php?id=1518 |website=The Michael J. Fox Foundation for Parkinson's Research |accessdate=28 July 2018}}</ref> Dr. Cuervo is also one of the founding members of the Women in Autophagy ([https://womeninautophagy.wixsite.com/site/about-wia WIA]) network dedicate to promote careers of young scientist interested in autophagy.

Cuervo was co-editor-in-chief of the [[Aging Cell]] journal from 2007 until  2021 and serves in the editorial board of [https://www.cell.com/cell-metabolism/advisory-board Cell Metabolism], [https://www.cell.com/molecular-cell/advisory-board Molecular Cell], [https://www.pnas.org/about/editorial-board PNAS] and [https://www.sciexplor.com/geromedicine/editorial_board Geromedicine].<ref>{{cite web |title=Ana Maria Cuervo, Ph.D, M.D |url=http://www.einstein.yu.edu/faculty/experts/8784/ana-maria-cuervo/ |website=Einstein Experts for Media |publisher=Albert Einstein College of Medicine |accessdate=26 July 2018 |archive-date=28 July 2018 |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20180728131345/http://www.einstein.yu.edu/faculty/experts/8784/ana-maria-cuervo/ |url-status=dead }}</ref> She has been involved in more than 300 publications.<ref>{{cite web |title=Ana Maria Cuervo, Ph.D., M.D. – Publications|url=https://einstein.pure.elsevier.com/en/persons/ana-maria-cuervo/publications/ |website=einstein.pure.elsevier.com |publisher=Elsevier |accessdate=28 July 2018 |language=en}}</ref> Dr. Cuervo has been included in the 2018, 2019, 2020 Highly Cited Researchers List (ranking of top 1% cited researchers).

== Research ==

|issue=1 |pages=53–66 |doi=10.1016/j.tem.2019.09.007 |issn=1879-3061 |pmc=7020649 |pmid=31699565}}</ref>.

As part of Cuervo's interest on the selectivity of autophagy, her group co-discovered with Mark Czaja and Rajat Sign the process of lipophagy<ref>{{Cite journal |last1=Singh |first1=Rajat |last2=Kaushik |first2=Susmita |last3=Wang |first3=Yongjun |last4=Xiang |first4=Youqing |last5=Novak |first5=Inna |last6=Komatsu |first6=Masaaki |last7=Tanaka |first7=Keiji |last8=Cuervo |first8=Ana Maria |last9=Czaja |first9=Mark J. |date=2009-04-30 |title=Autophagy regulates lipid metabolism |journal=Nature |volume=458 |issue=7242 |pages=1131–1135 |doi=10.1038/nature07976 |issn=1476-4687 |pmc=2676208 |pmid=19339967 |bibcode=2009Natur.458.1131S }}</ref>, which selectively mobilizes lipid droplets through autophagy, and with Laura Santambrogio co-discovered endosomal microautophagy (e-MI)<ref>{{Cite journal |last1=Sahu |first1=Ranjit |last2=Kaushik |first2=Susmita |last3=Clement |first3=Cristina C. |last4=Cannizzo |first4=Elvira S. |last5=Scharf |first5=Brian |last6=Follenzi |first6=Antonia |last7=Potolicchio |first7=Ilaria |last8=Nieves |first8=Edward |last9=Cuervo |first9=Ana Maria |last10=Santambrogio |first10=Laura |date=2011-01-18 |title=Microautophagy of cytosolic proteins by late endosomes |journal=Developmental Cell |volume=20 |issue=1 |pages=131–139 |doi=10.1016/j.devcel.2010.12.003 |issn=1878-1551 |pmc=3025279 |pmid=21238931}}</ref>, a selective mechanism for internalization of proteins into late endosomes/multivesicular bodies. Later Cuervo's group showed that e-MI cross-talks with CMA<ref>{{Cite journal |last1=Krause |first1=Gregory J. |last2=Kirchner |first2=Philipp |last3=Stiller |first3=Barbara |last4=Morozova |first4=Kateryna |last5=Diaz |first5=Antonio |last6=Chen |first6=Kuei-Ho |last7=Krogan |first7=Nevan J. |last8=Agullo-Pascual |first8=Esperanza |last9=Clement |first9=Cristina C. |last10=Lindenau |first10=Kristen |last11=Swaney |first11=Danielle L. |last12=Dilipkumar |first12=Shilpa |last13=Bravo-Cordero |first13=Jose Javier |last14=Santambrogio |first14=Laura |last15=Cuervo |first15=Ana Maria |date=2023-12-26 |title=Molecular determinants of the crosstalk between endosomal microautophagy and chaperone-mediated autophagy |journal=Cell Reports |volume=42 |issue=12 |article-number=113529 |doi=10.1016/j.celrep.2023.113529 |issn=2211-1247 |pmc=10807933 |pmid=38060380}}</ref> and that, as it is the case for CMA, eMI activity also declines with age<ref>{{Cite journal |last1=Krause |first1=Gregory J. |last2=Diaz |first2=Antonio |last3=Jafari |first3=Maryam |last4=Khawaja |first4=Rabia R. |last5=Agullo-Pascual |first5=Esperanza |last6=Santiago-Fernández |first6=Olaya |last7=Richards |first7=Alicia L. |last8=Chen |first8=Kuei-Ho |last9=Dmitriev |first9=Phillip |last10=Sun |first10=Yan |last11=See |first11=Stephanie K. |last12=Abdelmohsen |first12=Kotb |last13=Mazan-Mamczarz |first13=Krystyna |last14=Krogan |first14=Nevan J. |last15=Gorospe |first15=Myriam |date=October 2022 |title=Reduced endosomal microautophagy activity in aging associates with enhanced exocyst-mediated protein secretion |journal=Aging Cell |volume=21 |issue=10 |article-number=e13713 |doi=10.1111/acel.13713  |doi-access=free|issn=1474-9726 |pmc=9577956 |pmid=36116133}}</ref>. 

==Recognition==
Cuervo and her team have received numerous awards including the P. Benson Award, Keith Porter Fellow, Nathan Shock Memorial Award, Vincent Cristofalo Award in Aging, Bennett J. Cohen, Marshall Horwitz Prize, the Saul Korey Prize in Translational Medicine, the Juan Negrin Award on Physiology, the Spirit of Achievement Award, the SFRR-E Annual Award and the Howard Taylor Ricketts Prize. She has delivered prominent lectures such as the Robert R. Konh, the NIH Director’s, the Roy Walford, the Feodor Lynen, the Margaret Pittman, the IUBMB, the David H. Murdoxk, the Gerry Aurbach ,  the SEBBM L’Oreal-UNESCO for Women in Science, the Ronal Kohn, and the Harvey Lecture. She also received three times the LaDonne Schulman Teaching Award .<ref name="AECoM">{{cite web |title=Ana Maria Cuervo, M.D., Ph.D. |url=http://www.einstein.yu.edu/faculty/8784/ana-maria-cuervo/ |website=www.einstein.yu.edu |publisher=Albert Einstein College of Medicine |accessdate=28 July 2018 |archive-date=3 March 2017 |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20170303054502/http://www.einstein.yu.edu/faculty/8784/ana-maria-cuervo/ |url-status=dead }}</ref> In 2023, Cuervo was awarded Doctor Honoris Causa from the University of Buenos Aires. She was elected to the [[National Academy of Sciences]] in 2019.<ref>{{cite web |title=2019 NAS Election |url=http://www.nasonline.org/news-and-multimedia/news/2019-nas-election.html |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20190430143122/http://www.nasonline.org/news-and-multimedia/news/2019-nas-election.html |url-status=dead |archive-date=April 30, 2019 |website=www.nasonline.org |accessdate=30 April 2019}}</ref>

==Personal life==
Cuervo's husband was Dr. Fernando Macian, an immunologist at Albert Einstein College of Medicine, who sadly passed away in 2023. Cuervo and Macian were together since they met first year of Medical School in a research lab and continue collaborating scientifically through the years.<ref>{{Cite web |title= Cuervo am macian f - Search Results - PubMed|url=https://pubmed.ncbi.nlm.nih.gov/?term=cuervo+am+macian+f&sort=pubdate}}</ref>
